title: Dimension of a real self-similar attractor without exact overlaps
exact_target: For a finite nonempty real similarity family $\phi _i(x)=r_i$ $x+t_i$ with $0<|r_i|<1$, assume distinct nonempty words define distinct composed maps. If K is its compact attractor and $s>=0$ solves $sum_i$ $|r_i|^s=1$, must $dim_H$ $K=min(1,s)$, without any effective separation or algebraicity assumption?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
For a finite nonempty real similarity family $\phi _i(x)=r_i$ $x+t_i$ with $0<|r_i|<1$, assume distinct nonempty words define distinct composed maps. If K is its compact attractor and $s>=0$ solves $sum_i$ $|r_i|^s=1$, must $dim_H$ $K=min(1,s)$, without any effective separation or algebraicity assumption?

\subsection{Short English statement}
For a finite nonempty real similarity family $\phi _i(x)=r_i$ $x+t_i$ with $0<|r_i|<1$, assume distinct nonempty words define distinct composed maps. If K is its compact attractor and $s>=0$ solves $sum_i$ $|r_i|^s=1$, must $dim_H$ $K=min(1,s)$, without any effective separation or algebraicity assumption?
